text: Getting a protein shake onto a supermarket shelf takes three people. The rep who visits the store, the manager who runs the team, and the brand team who studies the shopper. RetailIQ gives each one a workspace. Let us follow one rep, Anita, through a single store visit.

Before the visit. Her day is ranked by a score she can argue with: how overdue each store is, its open tasks, and the revenue at risk. First stop, FreshMart Koramangala. Thirteen facings were agreed for the new chilled shelf plan. The last check found none in place.

Next, the pitch. AI writing a sales pitch normally invents numbers, and a buyer catches that instantly. So the rule here is cite, or stay silent. Every fact carries its source. Anything it cannot source is dropped.

And the sources open. Eleven are real published research. This one found out of stocks are still stuck near eight percent, despite everything bought to fix them. The sources invented for this demo say so, in the same panel.

She can also drop in the product flyer. The model reads what is on it. The protein claims, the proof points, the promotion. Those go into the pitch alongside the cited sources. Not a separate slide. The same argument, made stronger.

Then she rehearses. The AI buyer uses this store's real recorded objections, and they are hard. You want thirty percent of my shelf, for a brand that has never had one facing here. Tell me what I remove to pay for it.
With the live coach on, it reads the conversation while she types, before she sends anything, and gives her one line. Not a script. A prompt about the evidence she has not used yet.

Then a completely separate model scores her. The buyer never marks its own conversation, because one agent doing both is always kind to the rep. It quotes her own words, and names the evidence she had but did not use.

During the visit. This is real footage from a real supermarket, shot on a phone walking past the chiller. Protiva is a demo brand, so it will not be on a real shelf. The audit judges the brand that is, Hershey's, and on this shelf the brand earns its passes.

Another shelf, same brand, same rules, and this one does not pass clean. A competitor pack is wedged inside the brand's block, and packs are tilted. The score comes from the verdicts, so anyone can recount it.

She also counts by hand, because a camera misses things. The shelf is empty, but the system still says sixty four in stock. That is phantom stock. One study of twenty four thousand products found an eleven percent sales lift, and all of it came from fixing exactly this.

The order builds itself from what she just found, priced at trade value. Note the salads. Four day shelf life, so they are capped at four days of stock, not twenty one. Otherwise you are shipping waste.
After the visit. She writes two lines. It writes the summary, the commitments, the next actions with dates, and the record updates. The admin that normally eats the evening is gone.
Her manager sees the team instead. This rep is ahead on quota, but covering only three quarters of her territory. That is concentration risk, not performance. And it says who to coach, and why.
The shelf footage is real. The research is real and linked. The brand is invented, and labelled as invented. The score is calculated, not claimed. And where it does not know, it says so.
